title: Compactly generated exact localization source for a Grothendieck derived category
statement: Let A : Type uA be an abelian category with morphism universe vA, Grothendieck relative to w, with a chosen w-Hom derived category D(A) and coproducts indexed by Type max(w,vA,vH). There exists a category B with objects in Type max(uA,vA,max(w,vH)+1) and morphisms in Type max(w,vH), equipped with a zero object, an additive integer shift, a preadditive triangulated structure, and Type max(w,vH)-indexed coproducts. B is compactly generated [def-pc-compactly-generated]. There exist L : B → D(A), R : D(A) → B and an adjunction L left adjoint to R with invertible counit. L commutes with integer shifts and preserves distinguished triangles. This assertion is independent of any cohomological functor H and does not assert representability.

source.place: Tag 0F5V (injectives-lemma-gabriel-popescu), Tag 0F5X first paragraph; size extension by the free presentation and Baer criterion, Tag 05NU

proof.text: Choose a generator G and shrink its endomorphism ring (with the appropriate opposite) to w. Gabriel-Popescu supplies the small-module exact adjunction F left adjoint to U, with invertible counit. For a larger family A_i, the assumed coproduct P of A_i[0] in D(A) lies in D<=0: Hom(P,Y) is a product of zeros for every Y in D>=1. Truncation identifies Hom(P,X[0]) with Hom(H^0(P),X), making H^0(P) the required coproduct in A. For a larger module M, construct F(M) as the cokernel of the map of coproducts of G induced by its canonical two-step free presentation. This represents Hom(M,U(-)), hence extends the adjunction. It agrees with the original F on small modules, so its counit is invertible. If I is injective in A, U(I) is small-module injective by Gabriel-Popescu; Baer criterion (Stacks 05NU) tests only ideals of the w-sized ring, so its universe lift remains injective among larger modules. Adjunction and enough injectives show that the extended F preserves monomorphisms; right exactness follows from being a left adjoint.

Apply the exact localization termwise to complexes and pass to derived categories. Its shift comparison and preservation of distinguished triangles come from exactness. Compute the right derived adjoint using K-injective representatives. The termwise invertible abelian counit gives an invertible derived counit, as in Tag 0F5V.

The derived category of modules has coproducts indexed in Type max(w,vH). The free rank-one module in degree zero is compact: its shifted Hom groups compute cohomology, which commutes with sums of modules. These groups jointly detect acyclicity, so its shifted copies generate the derived category. Package the singleton family as compact generation.

Lift the object universe of the module derived category to max(uA,vA,max(w,vH)+1), leaving its Hom universe max(w,vH). Transport zero objects, shift, additive and triangulated structures, coproducts, compact generation, and the localization adjunction along the lifting equivalence. Package the structures and properties as the existential witnesses.
